Definition: a lot (as by means of a broken piece)
BiblicalUsage: Pur is a lot, cast as by a broken piece, to decide a fate. In the first month, they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, to find the day to destroy the Jews. Haman had cast Pur to destroy them, and that is why the days are called Purim, after the name of Pur.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lot is the proof that God rules chance itself: Haman cast Pur to choose the day of murder, and the lot chose the day of deliverance, because the lots are in the hand of the LORD. I hold that Purim is the feast of the reversed lot, where the enemy's day became the Jews' day.
